items.note: Mahishmati an important city and centre of trade by the Buddha's time, receding as Ujjain rose; regional trade-centre background.
Paramaras ruled parts of Nimar including Maheshwar but did not hold the town in much importance.
Plan of a Paramara-period temple at Un: pillared hall, shrine at back, carved porch, lofty shikhara built without lime or cement.
Shikhara 'adorned with clusters of miniature shikharas', described as common with Paramara temples.
Nilakantheshvar temple at Un: shikhara in common Paramara style; doorframes carved with Shiva and the Sapta Matrikas.
Un: about a dozen temples representing an architecture patronised by the Paramara kings of Malwa, Hindu and Jain.
Nemawar lay on the trade route from the north to the Deccan, mentioned by Albiruni in the early 11th century A.D.
Nemawar's Siddheshvar shikhara closely resembles the spire of the Nilakantheshvar Mahadeva temple at Udaypur; clusters of miniatures characteristic of Paramara temples of the 11th-12th centuries.
